repairs: Tekla DB1 cut frames. Tekla stores cuts that are square to a part with float noise (0.00024 rad seen). A flange cut 0.014° off a W27X84's own axes made the geometry kernel loop for hours on 44 versions of one model. Cut axes within 0.06° of the part's axes are now snapped exactly onto them; on three cut-heavy test models the output is identical (same parts, faces and extents; largest direction change 0.0033°).

Two IFC exports in one file. One IFC held a Tekla 16.1 model followed by a Tekla 20.0 joist model, both numbering entities from #1, so references resolved into the wrong model and nothing converted. Merged into one valid exchange structure (second block renumbered, one IfcProject so the millimetre unit applies) and converted: 12,848 parts.

Corrupt source coordinates. Four IFC files store points such as z = 2.6×10266. The exact-geometry path had written them into the STEP as unreferenced points (solids were correct, but the file's extent read as astronomical). Elements with such coordinates are now tessellated instead; part counts unchanged (5,588 / 5,052 / 4,910 / 5,356). Packaged copies replaced.

Elements that crash the geometry kernel. For IFC models that segfaulted, the crashing elements are found by bisection and left out; every other element converts. Each result lists the excluded elements by GUID.

IFC cut off mid-statement. A file whose last statement was only half written is repaired only when nothing else is missing: the unfinished statement is dropped and every reference must still resolve (a 284 MB Tekla 18.1 model lost 49 bytes of one property link).
Legacy IFC inputs. IFC2X2 / IFC2X files declared as IFC2X3 (accepted only when the whole file parses strictly), zipped IFC saved as .ifc, and unreadable headers normalised.
Worker fix. Jobs killed for memory are released immediately with a larger memory reservation; a type error had left them locked for 40 minutes.
